campaign: Integrated validation, phase 2: bounded capability gains and evidence-gated simplification
doctrine:
overgo improves models, and itself, through its own inference and training, unattended. Every row closes or speeds up the improvement loop (measure, find the gap, train or change, judge on held-out data, promote or revert), or directly serves inference or training; otherwise it is not filed. The milestone is the loop itself (improvement-loop): from there, the scorecard's gaps generate the work.

Finish partly landed rows before opening new ones. A consolidation reuses an existing owner and deletes the implementations it replaces in the same landing. A new shared component is allowed only when no existing owner can serve several real consumers, and it must remove more than it adds.

One meaningful run serves every obligation whose identity and contract match: it is written once, as one record with many readers. A run never judges what it produced.

A change's landing cost is read from its diff, not declared, as three independent effects, each checked against the diff: the lanes it reaches, whether it expires the inference-surface guards, and whether it needs a pinned-media reconciliation. Lanes are the main cost (20 minutes to over an hour a landing), so false lane reach is cut. A batch is one coherent change, normally one to three related rows, closed before it delays a user-facing result that is ready: an operating limit, not a gate. Before a batch lands, the packages its device lanes will run run on the device first, so a failure shows early. Guards are re-acquired once after the last surface batch of a run of them. Dependency work is verified twice, separately: its build and test closure, and the guard surface, which stops at overgodb and runrecord. A saving is the net recurring cost removed, after the replacement tests and their maintenance. A check retires only when its replacement covers the check's actual acceptance contract; the landing scorecard reports and never refuses, so it replaces no check. The gate writes all numbers; messages name causes, effects and what disappears.

Each row's rationale carries four plain lines: Serves (the loop stage, or the model or capability it runs or trains), Disappears (the owner reused, the implementations deleted, the tests retired or kept), Evidence (the run and record it reads or produces, and who else reads that record), Batch (the lanes its diff reaches, whether it expires the guards, and whether it needs a media reconciliation: three independent effects, each checked against the diff).

steps.rationale:
Owner review 2026-09-30: after the promotion rule and dev-loop-metrics land, run go run ./cmd/loop -improve once on the real store. It proves measure, compare, promote or refuse, and file gaps; it is not a train-and-improve cycle. items.title: Cut false lane reach: keep plan and loop edits out of the cuda lane

steps.title: Cut false lane reach: keep plan and loop edits out of the cuda lane
steps.rationale:
Owner review 2026-09-30: cut false lane reach. internal/plan and internal/loop sit inside the cuda lane's test closure, and each lane closure runs to 120–130 packages. So an edit to the plan tool or the loop driver pays the whole cuda lane (19 device packages at -p 1), although nothing there exercises the device.

Trim the test-only imports that pull large closures into the lanes, starting with the paths that bring internal/plan and internal/loop into the cuda lane's packages. Find them with go list -deps -test over the lane's packages. Each trimmed import either moves the test fixture that needs it into a package outside the lane, or replaces the import with the smaller owner the test actually uses.

Done when an internal/plan or internal/loop edit reaches no device lane: the gate's lane selection over such a diff names no lane.

Serves: loop speed. Disappears: false lane reach, and the hour-long landings it causes for host changes. Evidence: the gate's lane selection on a plan-only or loop-only diff. Batch: host; lanes: the ones whose closures shrink (cuda first).

Lanes (expected; the gate reads them from the diff): cuda first.

Re-scoped 2026-09-30 (owner review): the reach is verified from actual imports (go list -deps -test over each lane's packages), and each reaching import is classified: a test-only import is cut, while a production dependency stays and is noted as real reach, not false. Owners touched along the way get tests-pin-behaviour's trim. Ranked before goldens-own-parity: its saving is the smaller, clearer one, the whole cuda lane on every plan, loop and landing edit, and the gate's lane line now measures it.

items.title: Delete parity comparisons a golden duplicates; keep tests that run the implementation against goldens

steps.title: Delete parity comparisons a golden duplicates; keep tests that run the implementation against goldens
steps.rationale:
Goldens in git under one provenance manifest lock the ports, so the reference-comparison packages and their generators go.

Absorbed 2026-09-29, rationale kept:

goldens-provenance (Keep goldens in git under one provenance manifest and delete their Python generators):
- do, verify `go test ./internal/repoanalysis -run '^TestGoldensHaveProvenance$' -count=1`: Owner direction 2026-09-26. 177 tracked goldens (4.3 MB, the largest about 1 MB) stay where they are in git -- fixtures/ and package testdata -- because git is the durable, pushed copy, the store is local and has been rebuilt, a golden in git never makes its test skip, and moving them would churn the tests and the records that pin them. What they lack is provenance. One manifest in fixtures/ records, for each golden, its upstream repository and commit, its checkpoint identity, its input digest and its own digest; TestGoldensHaveProvenance refuses a golden without an entry or whose bytes differ from it. The upstream output itself is kept, not just a parity verdict: kernels legitimately move numbers, and only the upstream output re-checks parity after each move without re-running Python, where comparing against overgo's own old output would stack tolerances. The Python generators are deleted -- internal/parity/testdata/make_olmoe_tiny.py and those in tmp (timesfm3_golden.py, dinov2_golden.py, generate_kimi_k3_rank_reference.py and their inputs) -- because the manifest names what to re-run if upstream ever changes; no Python is tracked. The store holds only a future golden too large for git; none is today.

parity-packages-to-goldens (Delete the reference-comparison packages whose ports goldens lock):
- do, verify `go test ./internal/repoanalysis -run '^TestEveryTrackedFileHasAReader$' -count=1`: Owner 2026-09-26: once a port is locked by goldens, the reference-comparison packages go. internal/adaptiveparity, cmd/sensenovaparity and cmd/vqaparity have no production importer; each is deleted once the comparisons it runs exist as committed goldens with provenance (goldens-provenance: goldens stay in git). internal/audioparity is not pure comparison -- internal/mediacapability and cmd/webui-lane import it for ASR qualification and election -- so its production part moves to its owner and only its comparison part goes. No new rule: done when go list no longer finds the three packages and the tree still builds and vets. Check: the reader census, since deleting the packages must leave none of their fixtures or testdata behind; done also when go list no longer finds them.

Serves: inference correctness against locked goldens. Disappears: adaptiveparity, cmd/sensenovaparity, cmd/vqaparity, audioparity's comparison half and the Python generators; one provenance manifest remains. Evidence: the goldens in git. Batch: host (adaptiveparity reaches the cuda lane).

Lanes (expected; the gate reads them from the diff): cuda (adaptiveparity), audio (audioparity).

Re-scoped 2026-09-30 (owner review): delete duplicated comparisons only. Every port keeps a test that executes the implementation against its golden; a reference-comparison package goes only where such a test already covers what it compared, and its production part (audioparity's qualification) moves to its owner. The saving is stated as net recurring cost after the kept tests. Owners touched along the way get tests-pin-behaviour's trim.

media-campaign-one-record (Fold the media campaign's receipts into fewer committed records):
- do, verify `go test ./cmd/compatibility -run '^TestMediaCampaignIsOneRecord$' -count=1`: Owner decision 2026-09-26: evidence and reports stay committed to git, so the frozen media receipts are not moved into the store. The campaign spans 21 docs/image_video_*.json files, media_reviewed_deltas.json, media_report.json, MEDIA_REPORT.md and docs/media_samples; 15 receipts are read only by cmd/compatibility tests, each pinned by its own canonical-JSON digest constant (image_video_*_test.go via checkMediaProtocolIdentity), and image_video_merged.json carries the runtime_sha256 and runtime_paths the gate reads. The accepted-evidence audits still fail for another reason: TestAcceptedFP8Guard, TestRetiredGuardRecords and TestAcceptedGuardCatalog compare against accepted baselines that predate the realized-residency field ('baseline lacks realized residency', 'accepted cohort denominator differs: 0 distinct records'). items.title: Give the controller training cluster a train route on the shared run

steps.title: Give the controller training cluster a train route on the shared run
steps.rationale:
Split from wire-remaining-trainers on 2026-09-30. The controller training cluster is the one trainer family still reachable only from tests.

controllertrain.TrainSeed trains a scratch model and runs only on CUDA, through scratchmodel.ResidentTrainer. A train route on the shared run needs two things:
1. Scratch initial state in cmd/train/shared_run.go. The shared publish is fixed to InitialStateSpec{Model: session.model}, and it bootstraps its recipe from a weights file. A scratch model has no weights file, so the route needs the scratch construction as its initial state, as scratchmodel's own checkpoints record it.
2. TrainSeed must expose its trainer's OptimizerPlan, Snapshot and SaveWeights, like the other trainers, with a bit-exact round-trip test.

The route test is CUDA-only, so it runs in the cuda lane.

Serves: the train stage for the controller cluster. Disappears: the test-only entry path. Evidence: its first real run is its acceptance and its scorecard training cell. Batch: host, plus the cuda lane.

Lanes (expected; the gate reads them from the diff): cuda, device, integration.

items.title: Wire or delete dense-to-MoE upcycling

steps.title: Wire or delete dense-to-MoE upcycling
steps.rationale:
Split from wire-remaining-trainers on 2026-09-30. Dense-to-MoE upcycling (modelmerge.DenseToMoEArtifact over model.CompileDenseToMoERouter) is reached only by tests.

This is construction, not gradient training. The compiler derives centered, normalized expert centroids from activation evidence, and admits the router only when every held-out label wins with a strict routing margin. Nothing in the repository produces DenseToMoERouterEvidence, because there is no activation capture step.

A route needs:
- an activation-capture step over a dense model and a labelled corpus;
- the target model-definition artifact and its recipe;
- optionally, a trainable part such as a Muon router fine-tune, so the route publishes through the shared run like the others.

The owner decides whether upcycling belongs in the product. If it does, wire capture, compile and publish, then judge on the router's held-out margins. If not, delete modelmerge's dense-to-MoE path and model's router compiler.

Serves: the train stage (a MoE made from a dense model). Disappears: the test-only path, one way or the other. Evidence: the held-out routing-margin check the compiler already enforces. Batch: surface (internal/model).

Lanes (expected; the gate reads them from the diff): all (internal/model is surface).

Owner review 2026-09-30: the keep-or-delete decision comes first, against a measured gap; wiring waits on keep.

items.title: Train on unpaired preference feedback with KTO

steps.title: Train on unpaired preference feedback with KTO
steps.rationale:
Split from preference-loss-variants on 2026-09-30. ORPO and SimPO landed there as modes of the DPO objective. KTO does not fit the paired preference data shape.

KTO (Ethayarajh et al. 2024) is L = E[λ_y − v(x,y)], with r = log πθ(y|x) − log πref(y|x).
- The KL estimate z0 = max(0, mean of r over mismatched pairs (x_i, y_j), j≠i) is taken within a microbatch, with no gradient through it.
- For a desirable completion v = λ_D·σ(β(r − z0)); for an undesirable one v = λ_U·σ(β(z0 − r)).

What the current path lacks:
1. Unpaired data: records of prompt, completion and a desirable or undesirable label. This needs a new dataset kind and processor, plus its materialize path in trainingworkflow/data.go. The preference-token-pair processor, parsePreferences and trainingdata.PreferencePair all require a chosen and a rejected completion.
2. More than one prompt per step. unitBatchPolicy steps once per pair. KTO needs microbatches of at least 2, sequences spliced from one example's prompt and another's completion (scored under both policy and reference), and gradients summed across examples. sequenceGradientSum could extend to this.
3. λ_D and λ_U in PreferencePolicy. The paper advises λ_D·n_D / (λ_U·n_U) between 1 and 4/3.
4. A held-out judge for unpaired records, since the current slice scores pairs by DPO loss.

Do not substitute TRL's kto_pair: its matched-pair KL term carries gradient, so it is not the paper's definition.

Serves: preference training on unpaired feedback (thumbs-up and thumbs-down data). Disappears: nothing. Evidence: the held-out unpaired slice judges it. Batch: surface (densecausal, trainingprogram).

Lanes (expected; the gate reads them from the diff): all (densecausal and trainingprogram are surface).

Owner review 2026-09-30: ordered by user value and held-out availability. After e4b-full-parameter-trainer: its held-out unpaired preference set is still to be chosen.

items.title: Trace the model-level loop parts' consumers, then retire the unreached

steps.title: Trace the model-level loop parts' consumers, then retire the unreached
steps.rationale:
Filed 2026-09-30 when improvement-loop closed the loop through the scorecard: measure, turn gaps into rows, then judge on held-out data and promote or revert.

Model-level loop parts exist as separate pieces that the closed loop does not reach: strategy experiments, the improvement-fitness proof (cmd/loop -publish-fitness), rollout promotion, the circuit breaker, live rollback, quarantine re-entry, the autonomy ratchet and calibration. Together they are thousands of lines, each started by hand from cmd/recipe or cmd/seam-align.

Recommendation: delete what the loop does not reach, and re-file any part a real scorecard gap later calls for. The loop's own chain already covers promotion (scorecard-gated fast-forward of main) and rollback (refusal leaves main where it is). Keep only a part that a gap the loop has actually filed needs.

The alternative is to wire each part into the loop's promote step, for example rollout promotion behind the held-out verdict. That is the owner's decision, since the doctrine names these parts core.

Serves: the promote-or-revert stage. Disappears: the unreached parts, or their standalone entry points if wired. Evidence: deadcode and the loop's own chain (cmd/loop improve.go). Batch: host.

Lanes (expected; the gate reads them from the diff): cuda until lanes-false-reach lands.

Owner 2026-09-30: agreed, delete. The closed loop reused existing owners, so the unreached parts are exactly the limbo to cut.

Re-scoped 2026-09-30 (owner review): trace, then retire. Each part's real consumers are traced first (entry points, stored records it writes that something reads, tests only). Refusing to advance main is not post-deployment rollback, so the live-rollback and circuit-breaker parts are judged on their own consumers, not assumed covered by the loop. Small confirmed deletions can land earlier, with any batch that touches their owner.

items.title: Drill the recovery failures the loop has actually hit

steps.title: Drill the recovery failures the loop has actually hit
steps.rationale:
Re-filed 2026-09-30 (owner): failure-recovery was retired in the plan review, but it should be scoped to the recovery failures that have actually happened, not general drills. Each of these cost real landing time:
- A single browser test hung for 20 minutes at a wait whose condition the page could already show. The lane only ended at go test's timeout, with no page state. The wait mechanism is fixed (87944e765); the parked finding asks for page state when a wait ends without its predicate.
- A foreign gate, whose test stage is not serialized by the lane turn, loaded the GPU during this landing's lanes and refused it on a timing bound.
- Windows Defender quarantined the freshly built gate binary for hours. It is an owner-controlled setting, so the recovery is a background probe that re-checks the build and resumes landings, never an idle turn.
- A refused landing leaves the dirty tree in place. The stop gate keeps the turn open, but nothing yet records which refusal reason recurred.

For each: a drill that reproduces the failure deterministically (a test or a scripted scenario), the recovery the loop takes, and the signal that shows the recovery happened. Done when each observed failure has its drill passing.

Serves: unattended continuity of the loop. Disappears: the manual diagnosis each of these needed. Evidence: the gate's refusal records and lane logs. Batch: host; lanes: webui (the wait drill), none for the others.

Lanes (expected; the gate reads them from the diff): webui for the wait drill.

Consolidated 2026-09-30 (owner review) with device-claim-everywhere: one proof set. Cases come from actual incidents and uncovered invariants only. Ownership and isolation are proven (the foreign-gate case is the device-claim proof) before any GPU concurrency change. Concurrency is not a row: it is decided after dev-loop-metrics' lane attribution and the first lane reductions.

items.title: Have every GPU user take the device claim lanes wait on

budget.reason: the swap launcher's wait for device admission

steps.title: Have every GPU user take the device claim lanes wait on
steps.rationale:
Three sessions share one GPU. Preview servers started through launch.json hold the device while gate lanes time out behind them, and on 2026-09-23 a server of unknown origin was killed to free it. A served model should hold the same claim, so a lane waits for it and names it (01cbf544) instead of timing out. 2026-09-25: the device lane of 69368990 failed 'physical resource is already reserved' in devicemath while two other gate processes held the GPU, and passed unchanged on re-run; a claim every GPU user takes turns that into a wait with a named holder instead of a failed lane and a manual re-run. Found 2026-09-26: every CUDA context already takes the shared device claim (driver.ContextCreate calls processcontrol.ShareResource), so a served model holds it for its context's life, and a timed-out exclusive wait already names its holders (01cbf544, TestResourceWaitNamesItsHolders). What remains is proof, not mechanism: a device test that a served model's context holds the claim an exclusive reservation then waits on.

Serves: loop speed. Disappears: the unclaimed GPU users that cause lane refusals. Batch: host.

Lanes (expected; the gate reads them from the diff): device, model-journey.

Consolidated 2026-09-30 (owner review) with recovery-failures-seen: its remaining proof, a served model's context holding the claim an exclusive reservation waits on, is the ownership case of that row's foreign-gate drill, and lands with it.

lane-commands-folded (Fold the lane commands the gate does not call into test packages):

Fold what is still needed into test packages (train-lane's training routes keep running as tests: training is a capability, not a lane) and delete the rest. About 2k lines.

simplify-command-surface (Consolidate duplicated APIs and shipped binaries):
- do, verify `go run ./cmd/preflight && test -f internal/apimanifest/ownership_consolidation_test.go && go test ./internal/apimanifest -run '^TestOwnershipConsolidationContracts$' -count=1`: Rank duplicates by real callers and build, test, startup and packaging cost using command-discovery's inventory. Before starting, pick a concrete owner and bind the old-to-new caller map; migrate code, automation, manifests and docs in one batch and delete the displaced implementation and build target. A dispatcher over unchanged handlers does not count. Preserve public flags, schemas, exit codes, streaming, cancellation and evidence contracts. TestOwnershipConsolidationContracts rejects stale references and proves a smaller surface.

items.title: Move live-evidence acceptance tests off the landing path

steps.title: Move live-evidence acceptance tests off the landing path
steps.rationale:
Owner review 2026-09-27. Measured: 088a4774c's test stage re-ran 17 suites for 6 min 56 s (audioparity 376 s, cmd/compatibility 192 s, capabilityruntime 122 s, modelintake 119 s, server 71 s) because plan -stop had written a record into the live store at 17:56:23; the next plan-only landing, with no store write before it, ran 4 packages in 40 s. Suites that read the live store re-run on every store write, and their verdict depends on the machine's store rather than the commit. The gate runs go test with OVERGO_DATA_ROOT pointing at an empty scratch directory and OVERGO_AUDIO_REFERENCE_STORE unset (construction: no test can reach the live store through the environment); the 16 test files that name the store by path (overgodb-store, gitauthority.CanonicalOvergoDBDirectory) become hermetic on fixtures or scratch stores, or move off the landing path to the scheduled scorecard and validate, where live-store checks belong. Predicted effect: landings stop paying for store writes; a narrow landing's test stage stays near a minute. Measured 2026-09-27 before starting: with the data root pointed at an empty directory, 133 tests in 77 files across 12 packages fail (cmd/compatibility 32 files, internal/audioparity 19, internal/evaluation 10, speechsynth, server and others): retained-evidence acceptance tests and a few live model-file tests. They re-run when the evidence changes, which is correct; the measured 7-minute landing came from a control record (plan -stop) written into the evidence store, which stop-state-out-of-store removes. Moving them means splitting mixed files across 12 packages and a scheduled evidence run. Do it only if dev-loop measurement shows real evidence writes costing landings. Re-raised 2026-09-27 under landing-wall-budget: the four slowest suites a landing re-runs are these, and they re-run on dependency changes as well as store writes, so the stop-file fix alone does not bring landings under the budget. Updated 2026-09-27 after 32ad2b892: the store-write cause is gone. The data lives outside the module folder, so a store write re-runs nothing. The audio acceptances run in their own lane (780d83550). What remains is hermeticity: these suites' verdicts depend on the machine's data. That does not speed up landings, because a lane would run exactly when their code changes, as go test does now. So the row ranks after the user-visible fixes. Measured 2026-09-28 after the lanes landed: go test ./... with OVERGO_DATA_ROOT on an empty folder fails 92 tests in 12 packages: cmd/compatibility 56 (40 top-level accepted-evidence and acceptance projections, opening the store through retainedReferenceStore in 34 places and dataroot.Resolve in about 36), internal/evaluation 16, internal/speechsynth 7, internal/server 4, internal/audioparity 2, and one each in oscillatorimage, modelintake, dataset, capabilityruntime, cmd/smoke-lane, cmd/longform and cmd/benchmark-report. The work: consolidate each package's live-store entry into one helper behind testskip.StoreAcceptance, and run the packages in a store lane (without the five failing audits, tracked in refresh-accepted-evidence). The benefit is hermeticity only: with the data outside the module, a lane runs these exactly when go test does now. Ranked after plan-tool-plain-data.

Serves: loop speed. Disappears: live-evidence suites on the landing path. Batch: host.

Lanes (expected; the gate reads them from the diff): the lanes of the suites it moves.

Owner review 2026-09-30: justified as robustness unless the gate's timing shows a saving.

items.title: Carry the VAE lane's latent campaign surface until the lane closes it

steps.title: Carry the VAE lane's latent campaign surface until the lane closes it
steps.rationale: The overgo_vae lane (branch codex/overgo_vae, campaign overgo_rsi_with_vae, design docs/overgo_rsi_with_vae.md) runs the native-Go latent RSI and PEARL campaign with its own plan in its own worktree. Owner decision 2026-09-25: master takes the lane in parts that have a production consumer, not whole. Master ported the runtime part at e1ee1326fe2b (row vae-codec-stream-port: media.CodecChunkStream owning causal codec state, the Wan VAE host and CUDA encode and CUDA decode through it; the host streaming DecodeLatentVideo stays a test on master until it has a production caller); the ported files are byte-identical to the lane's, so merging master back is clean. DIRECTION FOR THE LANE when it merges master (master is in a consolidation-only phase: two birds with one stone, minimize to the maximum practical extent, no ledger where construction can prevent the object): (1) consumer first -- land each latent contract (representation latent state and codec, geometry, tensorstats resampling and robust scalars, media latent volume) together with its first production consumer; the first merge unit is first-latent-capability/existing-vae-inference-proof, and no export arrives without a caller; (2) no new record families -- express experimental evidence through the shared record table that automation-one-record-table builds instead of runrecord experimental_* families, and keep campaign-history adoption out of master's internal/plan; (3) reconcile pinned media runtime moves with a reviewed delta in docs/media_reviewed_deltas.json backed by a device receipt, never by narrowing TestReviewedDeltaRegistryExplainsTheTree; (4) never raise docs/clone_baseline.json -- the merged tree measured 7964 against master's 7991 while the lane raised it to 9970; (5) after merging master, drop the lane's testCodecChunkState copy in internal/media/codec_latent_test.go: master's TestCodecChunkStreamOwnsCausalState owns it; (6) keep evidence identities in compatibility.json refreshed from master's store, not the lane's. Master keeps its plan; any staged surface a later merge brings retires with this row. Done when the lane's campaign closeout has merged and TestVAECampaignClosedOut proves no staged entry names this row.
